questions.q: Who was the military commander and former slave who established the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty and laid the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate in 1206 CE?
questions.a: Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Delhi Sultanate in 1206 CE after the death of Muhammad Ghori. A wrong answer like "Ala-ud-din Khilji" reveals a chronological confusion between the early 13th-century founders and the late 13th-century imperial expansionists.

questions.q: Why did early rulers of the Delhi Sultanate choose Delhi as their capital instead of moving deeper into central India?
questions.a: Delhi held a crucial strategic location controlling the fertile Ganga-Yamuna Doab and major trade routes connecting Central Asia to the Indian heartland. A wrong answer assuming they chose it merely for religious reasons shows a failure to understand the military and economic geography of medieval statecraft.

questions.q: If a military commander in the 13th century relied heavily on loyal military slaves (bandagan) rather than hereditary nobles to run administration, what does this strategy reveal about their political challenges?
questions.a: It reveals that the ruler faced deep mistrust from existing nobility and local chiefs, forcing them to rely on carefully trained, loyal slaves who owed allegiance solely to the crown. A wrong answer indicating that slaves were chosen for cheap labor shows a misunderstanding of the high political status and trusted administrative roles of the *bandagan*.

questions.q: How did the accession of Razia Sultan to the throne of Delhi challenge traditional political norms of the 13th-century Islamic world in South Asia?
questions.a: Razia's rule challenged the patriarchal norms where leadership was strictly restricted to male military commanders, though her brief reign also exposed the fierce resistance from Turkish nobles (*Chahalgani*) who resented taking orders from a woman. A wrong answer claiming her rule was accepted peacefully without opposition indicates a superficial reading of court politics and gender dynamics in medieval chronicles.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "The establishment of the Delhi Sultanate was purely a religious conquest rather than a political restructuring of northern India." Defend your position with historical evidence.
questions.a: This statement is false because while religion played a role in identity, the primary motives and methods of the Sultans were political and economic consolidation—such as controlling revenue through the *iqta* system and suppressing rival regional chiefs regardless of their faith. A student who agrees with the statement fails to separate religious rhetoric from the practical administrative and financial goals of state-building.

questions.q: Construct a brief historical argument explaining why Iltutmish is considered the true consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate rather than Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
questions.a: A strong argument would point out that Aibak ruled for only four years and focused on basic military control, whereas Iltutmish institutionalized the state by introducing the silver *tanka*, organizing the *Chahalgani* (group of forty loyal nobles), and securing official recognition from the Abbasid Caliph. A weak answer merely lists dates of their reigns without linking institutional reforms to state consolidation.

Fill in the blank: Have you ever visited the Qutb Minar ______ in Delhi and wondered who built those towering monuments and why they chose Delhi as their capital?

What must you be able to do to master this topic?
